content: 1. Johnston et al. (2018) conducted a systematic review to investigate the relationships between training load, baseline characteristics, and the occurrence of musculoskeletal injuries and pain in endurance sports populations. Their findings were published in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport. 2. Lopes et al. (2012) explored the primary musculoskeletal injuries associated with running. Their comprehensive review was published in Sports Medicine. 3. Neubauer et al. (2016) reviewed the occurrence of stress fractures in the femoral neck among runners, providing an in-depth analysis of this condition in Research in Sports Medicine. 4. Nielsen et al. (2012) systematically reviewed the role of training errors in the development of running-related injuries. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy. 5. Qu et al. (2014) examined the association between physical activity and fracture risk, presenting their findings in the Journal of Bone and Mineral Research. 6. Saragiotto et al. (2014) identified the main risk factors for running-related injuries through a systematic review published in Sports Medicine. 7. Sobhani et al. (2013) conducted a systematic review on the epidemiology of overuse injuries in the ankle and foot among athletes, with their findings appearing in the Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports. 8. Tonoli et al. (2010) reviewed the incidence, risk factors, and prevention strategies for running-related injuries in long-distance runners, publishing their work in Sport & Geneeskunde. 9. Van der Worp et al. (2015) systematically reviewed the risk factors and sex differences in running-related injuries, with their findings published in PLOS One. 10. Videbæk et al. (2015) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the incidence of running-related injuries per 1,000 hours of running across different types of runners. Their work was published in Sports Medicine (Auckland, NZ). 11. Alentorn-Geli et al. (2017) examined the relationship between recreational and competitive running and the development of hip and knee osteoarthritis. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in the Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy. 12. Timmins et al. (2017) reviewed the association between running and knee osteoarthritis, presenting their findings in The American Journal of Sports Medicine. 13. Sommer et al. (2010) reviewed the potential link between bicycle riding and erectile dysfunction, with their findings published in The Journal of Sexual Medicine. 14. Lopes et al. (2011) conducted an observational study on musculoskeletal pain prevalence among recreational runners preparing for competition, analyzing data from 1,049 runners. Their findings were published in Journal of Physiotherapy. 15. Malisoux et al. (2015) explored the mechanisms underlying running-related injuries in their study published in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport. 16. Van Middelkoop et al. (2008) compared knee complaints in active sports participants versus non-sports participants in general practice. Their findings were published in BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders. 17. Ouzzani et al. (2016) introduced Rayyan, a web and mobile application designed to facilitate systematic reviews. Their work was published in Systematic Reviews. 18. Shea et al. (2009) validated AMSTAR as a reliable tool for assessing the methodological quality of systematic reviews. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. 19. Samitz et al. (2011) conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies to examine the relationship between physical activity and all-cause mortality. Their work was published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 20. Coenen et al. (2018) reviewed whether highly physically active workers have an increased risk of early mortality. Their meta-analysis included data from 193,696 participants and was published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine. 21. Wendel-Vos et al. (2004) conducted a meta-analysis of observational data to investigate the relationship between physical activity and stroke risk. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 22. Li et al. (2013) reviewed the association between physical activity and cardiovascular disease risk, presenting their findings in Current Opinion in Cardiology. 23. Sattelmair et al. (2011) conducted a dose-response meta-analysis to explore the relationship between physical activity and coronary heart disease risk. Their findings were published in Circulation. 24. Wolin et al. (2009) reviewed the role of physical activity in colon cancer prevention, publishing their meta-analysis in the British Journal of Cancer. 25. Mahmood et al. (2017) examined the relationship between domain-specific physical activity, sedentary behavior, and colorectal cancer risk in their systematic review and meta-analysis published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 26. Boyle et al. (2012) reviewed the association between physical activity and the risk of proximal and distal colon cancers, publishing their findings in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport. 27. Samad et al. (2005) conducted a meta-analysis to investigate the association between physical activity and reduced colorectal cancer risk. Their findings were published in Colorectal Disease. 28. Robsahm et al. (2013) reviewed the relationship between body mass index, physical activity, and colorectal cancer risk by anatomical subsite. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Cancer Prevention. 29. Wu et al. (2013) conducted a meta-analysis of prospective studies to examine the relationship between physical activity and breast cancer risk. Their findings were published in Breast Cancer Research and Treatment. 30. Pizot et al. (2016) reviewed the association between physical activity, hormone replacement therapy, and breast cancer risk. Their meta-analysis was published in the European Journal of Cancer. 31. Chen et al. (2019) conducted a meta-analysis of 38 cohort studies to investigate the relationship between physical activity and breast cancer risk. Their findings were published in Value in Health. 32. Voskuil et al. (2007) systematically reviewed the evidence on physical activity and endometrial cancer risk, publishing their findings in Cancer Epidemiology Biomarkers & Prevention. 33. Schmid et al. (2015) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to explore the relationship between physical activity and endometrial cancer risk. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Epidemiology. 34. Vermaete et al. (2013) reviewed the association between physical activity and lymphoma risk, publishing their meta-analysis in Cancer Epidemiology Biomarkers & Prevention. 35. Singh et al. (2014) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the relationship between physical activity and gastric cancer risk. Their findings were published in Cancer Prevention Research (Philadelphia). 36. Psaltopoulou et al. (2016) reviewed the association between physical activity and gastric cancer risk, publishing their findings in the Clinical Journal of Sport Medicine. 37. Chen et al. (2014) conducted a meta-analysis to investigate the relationship between physical activity and the risks of esophageal and gastric cancers. Their findings were published in PLOS One. 38. Behrens et al. (2014) reviewed the association between physical activity and gastroesophageal cancer risk, publishing their findings in the European Journal of Epidemiology. 39. Behrens and Leitzmann (2013) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to explore the relationship between physical activity and renal cancer risk. Their findings were published in the British Journal of Cancer. 40. Shephard (2016) reviewed the potential of habitual physical activity to reduce the health burden of renal cancer. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Applied Sports Sciences. 41. Krstev and Knutsson (2019) conducted a meta-analysis to examine occupational risk factors for prostate cancer. Their findings were published in the Journal of Cancer Prevention. 42. Shephard (2017) provided an updated review on the relationship between physical activity and prostate cancer, publishing their findings in Sports Medicine. 43. Liu et al. (2011) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate whether physical activity reduces prostate cancer risk. Their findings were published in European Urology. 44. O'Rorke et al. (2010) reviewed the potential of physical activity to modulate pancreatic cancer risk, publishing their findings in the International Journal of Cancer. 45. Bao and Michaud (2008) conducted a systematic review to explore the relationship between physical activity and pancreatic cancer risk. Their findings were published in Cancer Epidemiology Biomarkers & Prevention. 46. Keimling et al. (2014) reviewed the association between physical activity and bladder cancer risk, publishing their findings in the British Journal of Cancer. 47. Aune et al. (2015) conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to investigate the relationship between physical activity and type 2 diabetes risk. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Epidemiology. 48. McWilliams et al. (2011) reviewed occupational risk factors for knee osteoarthritis, publishing their meta-analysis in Osteoarthritis and Cartilage. 49. Gignac et al. (2019) systematically reviewed the relationship between occupational activities and the risk of developing osteoarthritis in the knee, hip, or hands. Their findings were published in Arthritis Care & Research (Hoboken). 50. Palmer (2012) reviewed the association between occupational activities and knee osteoarthritis, publishing their findings in the British Medical Bulletin. 51. White et al. (2017) conducted a meta-analysis to explore the relationship between domain-specific physical activity and mental health. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 52. Yang et al. (2018) reviewed the association between insomnia and job stress, publishing their meta-analysis in Sleep and Breathing. 53. Huai et al. (2013) conducted a meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies to investigate the relationship between physical activity and hypertension risk. Their findings were published in Hypertension.
